items.summary: Emails are used raw in signup (line 16), login (23) and forgot (30): no trim, lowercasing or normalisation, and no unique index is visible (no schema in repo). Case variants create duplicate accounts or failed logins.
items.fix: Normalise (trim, lowercase, Unicode NFKC) in one helper used by signup, login, forgot; add a unique index on the normalised email; use a validator such as zod.

items.summary: /forgot generates the reset token with Math.random (predictable), stores it in plaintext, sets no expiry, and never emails it. No reset-confirm route exists, so single-use and invalidation are not implemented. Email is also interpolated into SQL (injection).
evidence: searched: reset confirm route, expiry, token hashing in server.js
items.fix: Use crypto.randomBytes(32), store only a SHA-256 hash with a short expiry, make it single-use, and invalidate on use and password change. Parameterise the query. Prefer a hosted auth provider; a human engineer should review the flow.

items.summary: Passwords are hashed with unsalted MD5 at signup and login, which is trivially crackable.
items.fix: Switch to argon2id or bcrypt (argon2 / bcrypt package) with per-password salts; existing hashes need a rehash-on-login migration, so have an engineer handle it.

items.summary: Login returns the raw user id as the 'token'. There is no session, expiry, signature or revocation, and the id is guessable and sequential. Nothing validates it on other routes.
items.fix: Issue server-side sessions or signed JWTs with idle and absolute expiry and a revocation mechanism (session table or token version), or adopt a hosted auth provider. Human engineer should do this.

items.summary: No rate limiting on /signup, /login or /forgot, so credential stuffing and brute force against MD5 hashes are unrestricted.
items.fix: Add express-rate-limit with a shared store (e.g. Redis) per IP and per account on auth routes.

items.summary: No throttling, progressive delay, captcha or lockout of any kind on /login.
items.fix: Add per-account progressive delays or captcha after failures rather than hard lockout.

items.summary: Login returns a generic 'bad credentials' 401 for both unknown email and wrong password, and /forgot always returns ok. But /signup has no duplicate handling (would error or leak via a DB error), and the SQL injection in these routes undermines the guarantee. Timing is not equalised.
items.fix: Handle duplicate signup with a neutral response (and verification email), and fix the injection.

items.summary: There is no email verification step: signup inserts the account and it can log in immediately with any claimed address. No social login exists, but email is trusted for password reset and account identity unverified.
items.fix: Add an email_verified flag and a hashed, expiring verification token; block login, invites and linking until verified.
